question:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq:

1. He was the first Delhi Sultan to impose Jizya on Brahmins.

2. He abolished the hereditary character of iqtas.

3. He levied an irrigation (water) tax and also dug canals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: he was the first Sultan to extend the Jizya to Brahmins, following the advice of the ulema (फ़िरोज़ शाह तुग़लक़ — ब्राह्मणों पर जज़िया, सिंचाई कर)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: iqtas were transferable earlier, but the post was made hereditary in his reign.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: he imposed an irrigation tax and at the same time constructed irrigation canals and wells.

 

• He also created a PWD department and founded the cities Firozabad, Hisar, Fatehabad and Jaunpur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• He built Firoz Shah Kotla in 1354 as the fifth city of Delhi.

 

• Departments such as Diwan-i-Khairat, Diwan-i-Shifa, Diwan-i-Istiaq and Diwan-i-Bandagan were set up by him.

 

• He repaired the Qutub Minar and added the fifth storey.

 

• He is credited with founding around 300 cities.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Joining 1 and 2 accepts the false idea that he ended hereditary iqtas, which actually became hereditary under him, so the pair is wrong.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Joining 2 and 3 repeats the same error on iqtas, since the post became hereditary under him, and it also ignores the correct statement that he extended Jizya to Brahmins.

 

• Only 3 (Option 4): Taking only statement 3 leaves out his Jizya policy on Brahmins, which is well documented, so the set is incomplete.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Tughlaq dynasty:

1. It was founded by Ghazi Malik (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq).

2. The city of Tughlaqabad was built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

3. It ruled from 1320 to 1414.

4. Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah was its last ruler.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 3 and 4 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the dynasty was founded by Ghazi Malik, who took the name Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 (तुग़लक़ वंश — ग़ियासुद्दीन तुग़लक़)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: Tughlaqabad was built in Delhi by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq; Firoz Shah's city was Firozabad (Firoz Shah Kotla, 1354).

 

• Statement 3 is correct: the dynasty lasted about 94 years, 1320-1414, with nine rulers.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah was the last Tughlaq ruler, and Timur attacked in his time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghiyasuddin was killed in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed.

 

• Ibn Battuta believed Ghiyasuddin's death was arranged by his son Muhammad and the saint Nizamuddin Auliya.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq took over in 1325 and Firoz Shah in 1351.

 

• The Tughlaq phase was the longest of the Sultanate dynasties.

 

• The first Tughlaq Sultan, Ghiyasuddin, died in 1325, and his son Muhammad bin Tughlaq took the throne the same year; Firoz Shah, his cousin, followed in 1351.

 

NOTE

 

• 1, 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Selecting 1, 2 and 3 accepts that Firoz built Tughlaqabad, when the fortified city was founded by the dynasty's first Sultan, Ghiyasuddin.

 

• 2, 3 and 4 only (Option 3): Selecting 2, 3 and 4 also accepts the false Tughlaqabad claim and leaves out the correct fact about the founder, so it cannot be right.

 

• 1, 2 and 4 only (Option 4): Selecting 1, 2 and 4 again accepts Firoz as the builder of Tughlaqabad and drops the true 1320-1414 dating, making that combination wrong.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Lodi dynasty:

1. Bahlol Lodi founded the first Afghan dynasty to rule at Delhi.

2. Sikandar Lodi founded the city of Agra in 1504.

3. Ibrahim Lodi was defeated by Babur at Khanwa.

4. Bahlol Lodi did not sit on the throne but sat on a carpet with his amirs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Bahlol Lodi (1451-89) established the first Afghan dynasty at Delhi (लोदी वंश — बहलोल, सिकंदर, इब्राहिम)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 on the Yamuna, calling it Sikandarabad.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Ibrahim Lodi was defeated and killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat (1526); Khanwa (1527) was Babur's fight with Rana Sanga.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: Bahlol used to sit on a carpet with his Afghan chiefs, treating them as equals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikandar introduced the Ghaz-i-Sikandari measure, banned Tajiya and destroyed the Jwala Devi temple at Kangra.

 

• Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498 during his reign.

 

• Ibrahim Lodi ruled 1517-26 and was the last Sultan of Delhi.

 

• Gunpowder was first used in Indian warfare at Panipat in 1526.

 

NOTE

 

• 1, 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Choosing 1, 2 and 3 accepts that Khanwa saw Ibrahim's defeat, but that battle was fought in 1527 between Babur and Rana Sanga, long after the Lodi collapse.

 

• 2, 3 and 4 only (Option 3): Choosing 2, 3 and 4 includes the Khanwa mistake, since Ibrahim fell at Panipat in 1526 and Khanwa was Babur's 1527 fight with Rana Sanga, and it drops the true first-Afghan-dynasty fact.

 

• 1, 3 and 4 only (Option 4): Choosing 1, 3 and 4 includes the false Khanwa claim and leaves out the Agra foundation of 1504 which is a correct fact.

question:
Consider the following statements about Timur's invasion of India:

1. It took place in 1398 during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq.

2. Timur left Khizr Khan as governor of Multan before leaving India.

3. Timur established his own rule at Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Timur invaded in 1398 and sacked Delhi for three days while Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah was the Tughlaq ruler (तैमूर का आक्रमण, 1398)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: before withdrawing in 1399 he appointed Khizr Khan governor of Multan, and Khizr later captured Delhi.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Timur did not stay or found a dynasty at Delhi; he plundered it and returned to Central Asia.

 

• So only 1 and 2 are correct.

 

• Contemporary accounts describe the capture of Delhi as followed by a general massacre and plunder lasting several days, after which Timur marched out and the capital was left badly depopulated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• His invasion dealt a death blow to the Tughlaq dynasty.

 

• Thousands were killed and enormous wealth was looted.

 

• Khizr Khan established the Sayyid dynasty in 1414.

 

• The Sultanate continued as a much weaker state afterwards.

 

• Timur's capital was Samarkand, and he is also called Tamerlane; his invasion came about a century before the Portuguese voyage to India.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 (Option 1): Only statement 1 is incomplete because it leaves out the appointment of Khizr Khan, which is mentioned in the standard account of Timur's retreat.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing 2 with 3 accepts the false idea of a Timurid dynasty at Delhi while ignoring the correct dating of the invasion.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 4): Pairing 1 with 3 repeats the false claim of Timur's rule at Delhi and drops the correct Multan appointment, so it is not correct.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Qutub Minar:

1. The first three storeys are of red sandstone.

2. The fourth and fifth storeys use grey sandstone and white marble.

3. The Alai Darwaza is its southern gate, built by Alauddin Khalji.

4. It was completed entirely by Aibak.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the lower three storeys are of red sandstone (क़ुतुब मीनार — लाल बलुआ पत्थर और संगमरमर)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the fourth and fifth storeys use grey sandstone and white marble, reflecting Firoz Shah Tughlaq's repairs.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: the Alai Darwaza is the southern gate of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in the Qutub complex and was built by Alauddin Khalji.

 

• Statement 4 is incorrect: Aibak built only the first storey; Iltutmish added three storeys and Firoz Shah rebuilt the fourth and added the fifth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tower is about 73 m tall with a 14.32 m base.

 

• Lightning had damaged the upper storey before Firoz Shah's repair.

 

• Sikandar Lodi also renovated the structure.

 

• It is the tallest brick minaret in the world and a UNESCO site.

 

• The Qutub complex, with the Minar, the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the Alai Darwaza, is in Mehrauli, Delhi, and the iron pillar of the Gupta age also stands in the courtyard.

 

NOTE

 

• 2, 3 and 4 only (Option 2): Including statement 4 repeats the false claim that Aibak completed the whole tower; he got only to the first storey and three later rulers made the additions.

 

• 1 and 4 only (Option 3): Choosing 1 and 4 leaves out two correct statements and accepts the false claim of a single builder for the entire tower.

 

• 1, 3 and 4 only (Option 4): Choosing 1, 3 and 4 accepts Aibak's completion of the tower and ignores the correct description of the upper storeys' materials.

question:
Consider the following statements about taxes in the Delhi Sultanate:

1. Zakat was a religious tax on Muslims.

2. Jizya was a tax on Muslims.

3. Khums was one-fifth of the loot of war.

4. Usher was levied on non-Muslims.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Zakat was a religious tax on Muslims, at about 2-2.5 per cent (दिल्ली सल्तनत के कर — ज़कात, जज़िया, खम्स)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: Jizya was the tax on non-Muslims, which Firoz Shah Tughlaq extended to Brahmins.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Khums meant one-fifth of the plunder of war reserved for the Sultan.

 

• Statement 4 is incorrect: Usher was a 5-10 per cent levy on Muslims, not on non-Muslims.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kharaj was charged on non-Muslim cultivators.

 

• Lagan was an extra 2.5 per cent on Muslims and an extra 5 per cent on non-Muslims.

 

• Firoz Shah added an irrigation tax.

 

• Alauddin's discriminatory taxes included Ghari (house) and Chari (grazing).

 

• Alauddin Khalji's discriminatory levies included Jizya, Ghari and Chari, while Firoz Shah Tughlaq's list included Kharaj, Khams, Jizya, Zakat and an irrigation tax.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 4 only (Option 1): Selecting 2 and 4 does the opposite of the truth: it assigns Jizya to Muslims and Usher to non-Muslims, reversing both.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Selecting 1, 2 and 3 includes the false Muslim-Jizya claim, which wrongly places a non-Muslim tax on the Muslims.

 

• 3 and 4 only (Option 3): Selecting 3 and 4 accepts the Usher error, since that levy was taken from Muslims at 5-10 per cent, and also leaves out Zakat, which was undoubtedly a religious tax on Muslims.

question:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's conquests:

1. His first attack after becoming Sultan was on Gujarat in 1299, led only by Malik Kafur.

2. He captured Chittor in 1303 and it was renamed Khizrabad.

3. Malik Kafur led his army against Vijayanagara.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is incorrect: the Gujarat expedition (1299) was led by Nusrat Khan and Ulugh Khan, and Malik Kafur was bought there as a slave (अलाउद्दीन के अभियान — गुजरात, चित्तौड़)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Alauddin took Chittor in 1303 from Ratan Singh and renamed it Khizrabad after his son Khizr Khan.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Vijayanagara was founded only in 1336, long after Alauddin died in 1316, so neither he nor Kafur attacked it.

 

• Hence only statement 2 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Malik Kafur's expeditions reached Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.

 

• The poem Padmavat by Jayasi retells the Chittor story.

 

• Alauddin also fought the Mongols repeatedly.

 

• His capital was at Siri.

 

• Alauddin's southern expeditions took the Delhi armies beyond the Vindhyas for the first time on a large scale, reaching Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai under Malik Kafur.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 (Option 1): Only statement 1 is false because Malik Kafur was not the commander in Gujarat; he was purchased there during the campaign by the Sultan's generals.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Choosing 2 and 3 includes the false claim about Vijayanagara, a kingdom that came into being after the Khalji era had ended.

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 4): Choosing 1 and 2 accepts the false claim that the Gujarat expedition was led by Malik Kafur alone, though the notes name Nusrat Khan and Ulugh Khan.

question:
Consider the following statements about the iqta system:

1. It was a revenue assignment given in place of salary.

2. The holder was called Muqti or Iqtadar.

3. It was started by Balban.

4. The post of iqtadar was made hereditary under Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: an iqta was an assignment of land revenue given in place of salary (इक़्ता व्यवस्था — इल्तुतमिश द्वारा प्रारंभ)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the holder was called Muqti or Iqtadar, who led troops, kept order and collected revenue.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the system is credited to Iltutmish; Balban is known for Diwan-i-Arz and the destruction of the Forty.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: iqtadars were transferable, but the post was made hereditary under Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khalsa land was ruled directly by the Sultan, unlike iqta land.

 

• The land of the Sultanate was divided into large and small iqtas assigned to soldiers, officers and nobles.

 

• Iltutmish also created Diwan-i-Wizarat, linked with finance.

 

• A Muqti sent the surplus revenue to the Sultan after paying his troops.

 

NOTE

 

• 1, 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Choosing 1, 2 and 3 accepts that Balban began the system, but the notes and standard books credit Iltutmish with starting it.

 

• 2, 3 and 4 only (Option 2): Choosing 2, 3 and 4 accepts the false Balban attribution and omits the correct definition of the iqta as a salary substitute.

 

• 1, 3 and 4 only (Option 4): Choosing 1, 3 and 4 accepts the Balban error and drops the correct title of the holder, so it cannot be right.

question:
Consider the following statements about Raziya Sultan:

1. She was nominated as successor by Iltutmish.

2. The contemporary chronicler Minhaj-us-Siraj acknowledged that she was more capable than her brothers.

3. She was killed at Kaithal in 1240.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Iltutmish nominated his daughter Raziya as successor when his son Ruknuddin Firoz proved unfit, beginning hereditary succession in the Sultanate (रज़िया सुल्तान — इल्तुतमिश की उत्तराधिकारी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Minhaj-us-Siraj, author of Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, admitted that she was more capable than her brothers.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: after the revolt of Altunia of Bhatinda and her marriage to him, both were killed at Kaithal in Haryana in 1240.

 

• All three statements therefore hold true.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• She was the first and only woman Sultan of Delhi, ruling 1236-40.

 

• The people of Delhi had chosen her after rejecting Ruknuddin Firoz.

 

• She did not follow the purdah system and wore the kuba and kulah.

 

• Her reign is a key example of the struggle between the crown and the Forty.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Taking only 1 and 2 leaves out her death at Kaithal after the Altunia revolt, which is an established fact of her reign.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Taking only 2 and 3 leaves out her nomination by Iltutmish, an equally valid fact about the transition from Iltutmish to Raziya.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Taking only 1 and 3 leaves out Minhaj's testimony, which is a standard reference in discussions of the Sultanate's only woman ruler.

question:
Match the rulers with their works.

Column A: (a) Qutbuddin Aibak (b) Iltutmish (c) Alauddin Khalji (d) Firoz Shah Tughlaq

Column B: (i) Alai Darwaza (ii) Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Delhi (iii) Tomb of Sultan Ghari (iv) Firoz Shah Kotla
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aibak began the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque at Delhi, so a matches ii (दिल्ली सल्तनत की इमारतें — शासक और निर्माण)

 

• Iltutmish built the tomb of Sultan Ghari for his eldest son, which is why his period is called the Era of Tombs: b matches iii.

 

• Alauddin Khalji added the Alai Darwaza, the southern gate of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque: c matches i.

 

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq built Firoz Shah Kotla in 1354 as the fifth city of Delhi: d matches iv.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aibak also built Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra at Ajmer.

 

• Alauddin's other works include Siri fort and the Alai Minar, which remained incomplete.

 

• Balban's building is the Lal Mahal and an Islamic-style tomb.

 

• Firoz Shah also founded Firozabad, Hisar, Fatehabad and Jaunpur.

 

• Siri, Alauddin's capital, was the second city of medieval Delhi, after the Qila Rai Pithora area, followed by Tughlaqabad and later Firozabad.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 1): This key swaps Aibak's mosque with Iltutmish's tomb, wrongly crediting Iltutmish with the mosque and Aibak with the Sultan Ghari tomb, which came decades later.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv (Option 3): This key gives the Alai Darwaza to Iltutmish and the Sultan Ghari tomb to Alauddin, though the Darwaza was built by Alauddin and the tomb by Iltutmish.

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i (Option 4): This key swaps Alauddin's Alai Darwaza with Firoz Shah's Kotla, which is wrong because Firoz Shah's work is the 1354 fortress and Alauddin's work is the gateway.

question:
Match the departments with the Sultans linked to them.

Column A: (a) Diwan-i-Arz (b) Diwan-i-Mustakhraj (c) Diwan-i-Amir Kohi (d) Diwan-i-Khairat

Column B: (i) Muhammad bin Tughlaq (ii) Alauddin Khalji (iii) Balban (iv) Firoz Shah Tughlaq
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diwan-i-Arz, the military department, is linked with Balban: a-iii (दीवान-ए-अर्ज़ — बलबन)

 

• Diwan-i-Mustakhraj, which collected arrears of revenue and checked corruption, is linked with Alauddin Khalji: b-ii.

 

• Diwan-i-Amir Kohi, the agriculture department, was set up by Muhammad bin Tughlaq: c-i.

 

• Diwan-i-Khairat, for donations toward widows and orphans, was set up by Firoz Shah Tughlaq: d-iv.

 

• These departments show how the Sultanate's administration grew by layers, each major ruler adding offices fitted to his own priorities, such as defence, revenue discipline, farming or welfare.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diwan-i-Wizarat, the finance department, is linked with Iltutmish.

 

• Diwan-i-Insha was the department of correspondence.

 

• Firoz Shah also set up Diwan-i-Bandagan, Diwan-i-Shifa and Diwan-i-Istiaq.

 

• The Wazir headed the finance department.

 

• The Wazir headed the finance department, and Diwan-i-Insha handled correspondence, giving the Sultanate a core of established ministries.

 

NOTE

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv (Option 1): This key gives the military department to Alauddin and the arrears department to Balban, reversing the two; arrears collection was Alauddin's initiative and the army office is Balban's.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv (Option 2): This key gives the agriculture department to Alauddin and the arrears department to Muhammad bin Tughlaq, but the Mustakhraj belongs to Alauddin and the Kohi to Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 4): This key gives the military department to Firoz Shah and charity to Balban, which is false because the Khairat was Firoz Shah's welfare initiative and Diwan-i-Arz belongs to Balban.

question:
Match the dynasties with their founders.

Column A: (a) Slave dynasty (b) Khalji dynasty (c) Sayyid dynasty (d) Lodi dynasty

Column B: (i) Bahlol Lodi (ii) Khizr Khan (iii) Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji (iv) Qutbuddin Aibak
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Slave dynasty (1206-90) was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak: a-iv (वंश और संस्थापक — दिल्ली सल्तनत)

 

• The Khalji dynasty (1290-1320) was founded by Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji: b-iii.

 

• The Sayyid dynasty (1414-51) was founded by Khizr Khan, Timur's governor of Multan: c-ii.

 

• The Lodi dynasty (1451-1526) was founded by Bahlol Lodi, the first Afghan dynasty at Delhi: d-i.

 

• Both the Slave and Khalji dynasties belong to the thirteenth century, while the Sayyid and Lodi dynasties belong to the fifteenth, so the founders can be separated by period as well as by name.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tughlaq dynasty was founded by Ghazi Malik (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) in 1320.

 

• The Tughlaq dynasty lasted about 94 years with nine rulers.

 

• Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan, died at Panipat in 1526.

 

• Alam Shah, the last Sayyid, abdicated for Bahlol.

 

• The Slave dynasty ended in 1290 with Kaiqubad, and the Khaljis ended in 1320 when Ghazi Malik removed the last Khalji ruler.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 1): This key exchanges the founders of the Slave and Khalji dynasties, giving Jalaluddin the Slave line and Aibak the Khalji line, which are chronologically reversed.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i (Option 3): This key exchanges the Sayyid and Khalji founders, placing Khizr Khan at the head of the Khalji line, though he belongs to the post-Timur period of 1414.

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii (Option 4): This key exchanges the Sayyid and Lodi founders, making Bahlol the Sayyid founder and Khizr Khan the Lodi founder, though the Lodis followed the Sayyids.

question:
Match the rulers with their capitals or seats.

Column A: (a) Qutbuddin Aibak (b) Alauddin Khalji (c) Muhammad bin Tughlaq (d) Sikandar Lodi

Column B: (i) Agra (ii) Daulatabad (iii) Lahore (iv) Siri
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aibak ruled from Lahore, not Delhi: a-iii (शासक और राजधानी — ऐबक: लाहौर)

 

• Alauddin Khalji built the new town and fort of Siri and made it his capital: b-iv.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq transferred the capital to Devagiri, renamed Daulatabad, in 1327: c-ii.

 

• Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and later made it his capital: d-i.

 

• A useful check is geography: Lahore lies in the north-west, Siri and Agra in the north, and Daulatabad far to the south in the Deccan, near present-day Aurangabad in Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Daulatabad was a failed experiment that wasted money and damaged the Sultan's prestige.

 

• Tughlaqabad and Firozabad were separate Delhi cities.

 

• Sikandar also called the new city Sikandarabad.

 

• Iltutmish is regarded as the Sultan who made Delhi the capital.

 

• Daulatabad's fortress in Maharashtra stands on a hill and is known for its defensive design, which impressed even contemporary writers.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i (Option 1): This key gives Daulatabad to Alauddin and Siri to Muhammad bin Tughlaq, reversing two capitals that are well known and not interchangeable.

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i (Option 2): This key gives Siri to Aibak and Lahore to Alauddin, whereas Lahore was Aibak's seat and Siri was Alauddin's new town.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii (Option 4): This key gives Agra to Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Daulatabad to Sikandar Lodi, a pairing that misplaces both rulers by roughly a century and a half.

question:
Match the events with their years.

Column A: (a) Timur captures Delhi (b) Siege of Chittor by Alauddin Khalji (c) Vasco da Gama reaches India (d) Capital moved to Devagiri

Column B: (i) 1303 (ii) 1327 (iii) 1398 (iv) 1498
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Timur captured Delhi in 1398: a-iii (घटनाएँ और वर्ष — तैमूर 1398)

 

• Alauddin Khalji's siege and capture of Chittor took place in 1303: b-i.

 

• Vasco da Gama reached India on 17 May 1498, during Sikandar Lodi's reign: c-iv.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital to Devagiri in 1327: d-ii.

 

• The gap between 1398 and 1498 is exactly a century, and both the Chittor siege and the Devagiri transfer lie in the first half of the fourteenth century, which makes elimination easy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Timur left India in 1399 after plundering Delhi.

 

• The token currency followed in 1329.

 

• Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504.

 

• The First Battle of Panipat took place in 1526.

 

• The 1498 landing at Calicut began the sea route between Europe and India, which later changed the political history of the subcontinent.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i (Option 1): This key swaps the Chittor and Devagiri years, placing the capital transfer in 1303 and the siege in 1327, which reverses two known dates.

 

• a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii (Option 3): This key gives Timur the year 1498 and Vasco da Gama 1398; the two dates are exchanged and the gap of a century makes the pairing incorrect.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv (Option 4): This key gives Vasco da Gama the year 1327 and the capital move 1498, even though the Portuguese voyage belongs to the Lodi period and the capital shift to the Tughlaq era.

question:
Arrange the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate in chronological order of their reigns:

1. Balban

2. Raziya Sultan

3. Qutbuddin Aibak

4. Iltutmish
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3-4-2-1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-10) came first as founder of the Slave dynasty, followed by Iltutmish (1211-36), then Raziya (1236-40) and finally Balban (1265/66-87) (क्रम: ऐबक, इल्तुतमिश, रज़िया, बलबन)

 

• Aram Shah held the throne for about eight months between Aibak and Iltutmish.

 

• Between Raziya and Balban several weak Sultans, including Nasiruddin Mahmud, ruled in the 1240s-60s.

 

• The correct order of the four given rulers is therefore 3-4-2-1.

 

• Raziya's dates (1236-40) lie between Iltutmish's and Balban's, with Aram Shah and several short-lived rulers filling the gaps in the early years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raziya was removed from the throne in 1240 and killed at Kaithal.

 

• Balban was also known as Ulugh Khan and took the title Zill-i-Ilahi.

 

• After Balban, his grandson Kaiqubad ruled 1287-90 and the Slave dynasty ended.

 

• Iltutmish nominated Raziya as his successor.

 

• The Sultanate's era of the Slave rulers began in 1206 and ended in 1290, spanning eighty-four years in all.

 

NOTE

 

• 3-2-4-1 (Option 1): Placing Raziya before Iltutmish is impossible, since she took the throne only after her father's death in 1236, and Aibak's immediate successor was Aram Shah and then Iltutmish.

 

• 4-3-2-1 (Option 2): Placing Iltutmish first ignores that Aibak founded the Sultanate in 1206, before Iltutmish seized the throne in 1211, so this order starts the sequence incorrectly.

 

• 3-4-1-2 (Option 3): Placing Balban before Raziya reverses their reigns; Balban became Sultan in the 1260s, a quarter century after Raziya's death in 1240.

question:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order of accession:

1. Firoz Shah Tughlaq

2. Alauddin Khalji

3. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq

4. Jalaluddin Khalji
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4-2-3-1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji came first in 1290 as founder of the Khalji line, followed by Alauddin Khalji (1296), then Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (1320) and finally Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351) (क्रम: जलालुद्दीन, अलाउद्दीन, ग़ियासुद्दीन, फ़िरोज़)

 

• Alauddin took the throne by murdering Jalaluddin at Kara.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, formerly Ghazi Malik, started the Tughlaq dynasty in 1320.

 

• Between Ghiyasuddin and Firoz Shah came Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-51).

 

• Jalaluddin's reign was short (1290-96), Alauddin's lasted twenty years (1296-1316), and the Tughlaq line followed after the brief Khalji successors had been removed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji founded the dynasty in 1290.

 

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq ruled until 1388 and built Firoz Shah Kotla in 1354.

 

• Alauddin ruled until 1316.

 

• The Tughlaq dynasty lasted until 1414.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq stands between Ghiyasuddin and Firoz in the Tughlaq order, with his reign running 1325-51. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq ruled only five years, 1320-25, but founded the dynasty that lasted until 1414 and built Tughlaqabad.

 

NOTE

 

• 2-4-3-1 (Option 1): Putting Alauddin before Jalaluddin ignores that Alauddin seized the throne by killing Jalaluddin in 1296, so the uncle necessarily preceded the nephew.

 

• 4-3-2-1 (Option 3): Putting Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq before Alauddin Khalji places the Tughlaqs before the Khaljis, whereas the Khalji dynasty ended in 1320 when Ghazi Malik took over.

 

• 4-2-1-3 (Option 4): Putting Firoz Shah before Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq reverses the Tughlaq order, as Firoz succeeded Muhammad bin Tughlaq a quarter century after the founder's accession.

question:
Arrange the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in chronological order:

1. Sayyid

2. Khalji

3. Lodi

4. Tughlaq
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2-4-1-3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khalji dynasty began in 1290, the Tughlaq in 1320, the Sayyid in 1414 and the Lodi in 1451, giving the order 2-4-1-3 (वंशों का क्रम: खिलजी, तुग़लक़, सैयद, लोदी)

 

• The Slave dynasty (1206-90) preceded all four.

 

• Timur's invasion of 1398 separates the Tughlaq and Sayyid periods and led to Khizr Khan's rise.

 

• The Lodis ended in 1526 when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat.

 

• Between the dynasties there were short transitions: Khusrau Khan's brief rule ended the Khaljis, and Timur's 1398 raid and the rise of Khizr Khan bridged the Tughlaq and Sayyid periods.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sayyid dynasty had four rulers and a small domain around Delhi.

 

• Lodi rule is called the first Afghan dynasty of India.

 

• The Tughlaq dynasty ran 1320-1414, about 94 years.

 

• Alam Shah, the last Sayyid, gave up the throne to Bahlol Lodi.

 

• The Sultanate's five dynasties together ruled from 1206 until 1526, a period of about three hundred and twenty years.

 

NOTE

 

• 4-2-1-3 (Option 1): Putting Tughlaq before Khalji reverses the first two dynasties; the Khaljis came first under Jalaluddin in 1290 and the Tughlaqs in 1320.

 

• 2-4-3-1 (Option 2): Putting Lodi before Sayyid is wrong because the Sayyids ruled 1414-51 and Bahlol Lodi accepted the throne from the last Sayyid in 1451.

 

• 2-1-4-3 (Option 4): Putting Sayyid before Tughlaq overlooks that Khizr Khan became ruler only after Timur's invasion destroyed Tughlaq power, so the Tughlaqs must come first.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

1. Vasco da Gama's arrival in India

2. Founding of Agra by Sikandar Lodi

3. First Battle of Panipat

4. Bahlol Lodi becomes Sultan of Delhi
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4-1-2-3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bahlol Lodi became Sultan in 1451, Vasco da Gama reached India on 17 May 1498, Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and the First Battle of Panipat took place in 1526 (घटनाओं का क्रम: 1451, 1498, 1504, 1526)

 

• The order is therefore 4-1-2-3.

 

• Sikandar was the ruler of Delhi at the time of Vasco da Gama's landing at Calicut.

 

• Panipat ended the Sultanate and began Mughal rule.

 

• Panipat (1526) ended the Lodi line and the Sultanate, thus completing the whole sequence of events in the list from 1451 to 1526.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikandar named the new city Sikandarabad and made it his capital in 1506.

 

• Bahlol ruled for 38 years, the longest period among Delhi Sultans.

 

• Ibrahim Lodi died fighting Babur.

 

• Portuguese contact with India was thereafter established along the west coast.

 

• Gunpowder artillery, introduced by Babur at Panipat, changed the nature of warfare in north India after 1526.

 

NOTE

 

• 1-4-2-3 (Option 2): Starting with Vasco da Gama's arrival overlooks that Bahlol Lodi became Sultan nearly half a century earlier, in 1451, so the order of the first two events is reversed.

 

• 4-2-1-3 (Option 3): Placing Agra's foundation before Vasco da Gama's arrival wrongly dates the founding of Agra, which came in 1504, six years after the Portuguese landing of 1498.

 

• 4-1-3-2 (Option 4): Placing Panipat before the founding of Agra is wrong because Ibrahim Lodi's defeat in 1526 came more than two decades after Sikandar Lodi founded the city.

question:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji introduced strict price control in the markets of Delhi.

Reason (R): He maintained a large standing army that was paid regular cash salaries.
option_1: A and R are both true, but R does not explain A
option_2: A is true, but R is false
option_3: A is false, but R is true
option_4: A and R are both true, and R explains A
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and R are both true, and R explains A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: Alauddin Khalji fixed prices of grain, cloth, horses, slaves and other goods in four Delhi markets under the Shahna-i-Mandi and the Diwan-i-Riyasat (अलाउद्दीन की मूल्य नियंत्रण नीति)

 

• Reason R is true: he maintained a large permanent army and paid soldiers in cash rather than by land grants.

 

• R explains A: cash salaries went further only if essential goods were cheap, so paying soldiers in cash led directly to price regulation.

 

• The Dagh and Huliya systems kept the army efficient.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Banjaras supplied grain to the city, and black marketing was strictly forbidden.

 

• The Mongol threat was one reason for such a large force.

 

• A separate department, Diwan-i-Mustakhraj, collected arrears of revenue.

 

• The policy is the reason Alauddin is known for his Market Reform.

 

• Malik Kafur's southern campaigns and the Mongol repulses used a standing army that Alauddin could afford only with low prices.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are both true, but R does not explain A (Option 1): Saying that R does not explain A overlooks the direct link: cash pay and low prices were two parts of a single scheme to support a big army.

 

• A is true, but R is false (Option 2): Calling R false denies the cash salary system, a well-established feature of Alauddin's army policy, so this verdict conflicts with a basic and widely known fact of his reign.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 3): Calling A false denies price control, which is the best-known reform of Alauddin's reign and the very reason he is remembered for his Market Reforms in the standard accounts.

question:
Assertion (A): The Delhi Sultanate escaped invasion by Chengiz Khan during Iltutmish's reign.

Reason (R): Iltutmish's Chahalgani nobles defeated Chengiz Khan in a decisive battle.
option_1: A and R are both true, and R explains A
option_2: A and R are both true, but R does not explain A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: when Chengiz Khan pursued the fugitive Khwarazmian prince, Iltutmish refused him shelter, and the Mongol leader turned back without entering India (मंगोल नीति — इल्तुतमिश ने चंगेज़ ख़ाँ से भारत को बचाया)

 

• Reason R is false: no battle was fought; Chengiz Khan simply returned home, so the Chahalgani did not defeat him.

 

• The Turkan-i-Chahalgani (Group of Forty) was formed to deal with Mongol attacks and also became a powerful block of nobles.

 

• The Mongol policy of Iltutmish saved India from Chengiz Khan's wrath.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Temujin, known as Chengiz Khan, was the leader of the Mongols who began invading Central Asia.

 

• Alauddin Khalji later faced repeated Mongol invasions and defended successfully.

 

• Balban later destroyed the Forty.

 

• Iltutmish ruled 1211-36.

 

• Iltutmish received a robe of honour and a letter of investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229, which gave his rule a legal standing.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are both true, and R explains A (Option 1): The pair is not true together because R is false: the Mongols were never beaten in a decisive battle by the Forty, and Chengiz Khan turned back on his own.

 

• A and R are both true, but R does not explain A (Option 2): The pair is not both true with a missing link, because R is simply false as a historical claim, not just an unrelated true statement.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 4): A is not false: the Sultanate was not invaded by Chengiz Khan, and the reason for it was Iltutmish's careful diplomacy.

question:
Assertion (A): The Turkish nobles accepted Raziya's rule without opposition.

Reason (R): She gave up female dress, wore kuba and kulah and held court with her face unveiled.
option_1: A and R are both true, and R explains A
option_2: A is false, but R is true
option_3: A and R are both true, but R does not explain A
option_4: A is true, but R is false
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is false, but R is true.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is false: many Turkish nobles resented a woman ruler, and Altunia of Bhatinda, among others, rose against her, which led to her death at Kaithal in 1240 (रज़िया सुल्ताना — तुर्की अमीरों का विरोध)

 

• Reason R is true: she wore the kuba (coat) and kulah (cap), rejected purdah and held court unveiled.

 

• She was chosen by the people of Delhi after the nobles rejected her brother.

 

• Her style of rule was one of the reasons for the nobles' dislike of her.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• She is the first and only woman Sultan of Delhi.

 

• Minhaj-us-Siraj noted she was more capable than her brothers.

 

• Iltutmish had nominated her as heir.

 

• Her reign lasted from 1236 to 1240.

 

• Altunia of Bhatinda, the Abyssinian Yaqut and the Forty were different strands in the opposition to the rule of Raziya.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are both true, and R explains A (Option 1): The claim that both are true and R explains A fails because A is false; the nobles did oppose her.

 

• A and R are both true, but R does not explain A (Option 3): The claim that both are true but unrelated also fails because A is false, since the Turkish nobility revolted rather than accepted her.

 

• A is true, but R is false (Option 4): The claim that A is true but R is false reverses the facts: Raziya did adopt male dress and an unveiled court, while her opponents were strong.

question:
Assertion (A): Firoz Shah Tughlaq is regarded as a great city-builder among the Delhi Sultans.

Reason (R): He repaired the Qutub Minar after it was struck by lightning.
option_1: A and R are both true, but R does not explain A
option_2: A and R are both true, and R explains A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and R are both true, but R does not explain A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: he is credited with founding some 300 cities, including Firozabad, Hisar, Fatehabad and Jaunpur, and built Firoz Shah Kotla in 1354 (फ़िरोज़ शाह तुग़लक़ — नगर निर्माता)

 

• Reason R is also true: he reconstructed the fourth storey of the Qutub Minar after lightning damage and added the fifth.

 

• R does not explain A: repairing an existing tower is a building act but it is not why he is known as the founder of cities.

 

• Fatehabad was named after his son Fateh Khan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• He created the first PWD department.

 

• He dug canals and wells but also imposed an irrigation tax.

 

• His Diwan-i-Khairat gave aid for marriages of poor girls.

 

• Jaunpur is called the Shiraz of the East.

 

• Jaunpur, another city associated with Firoz Shah, later became an independent Sharqi kingdom and a centre of learning.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are both true, and R explains A (Option 2): The claim that R explains A fails since repairing one tower cannot account for founding hundreds of cities; the two facts are true but belong to separate areas of his activity.

 

• A is true, but R is false (Option 3): The claim that A is true but R is false is incorrect because the lightning repair of the Minar is a recorded fact.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 4): The claim that A is false is incorrect because Firoz Shah's city-founding activity is among the best known features of his rule.

question: Which of the following was NOT one of the ambitious projects of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Market control with fixed prices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Market control with fixed prices belongs to Alauddin Khalji, so it is not a project of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (मार्केट सुधार — अलाउद्दीन ख़िलजी)

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq's five projects were the transfer of capital (1327), token currency (1329), Doab taxation, agricultural reforms (Diwan-i-Amir Kohi) and the Khurasan-Qarachil expedition (1339-40).

 

• All five ended in failure, because they were far ahead of their time and were poorly executed.

 

• The failures damaged the Sultan's prestige and drained the treasury.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq was known as Juna Khan and Ulugh Khan.

 

• He appointed people from humble professions to high posts.

 

• Alauddin's market policy was based on cash-paid soldiers.

 

• Ibn Battuta visited India during his reign.

 

• The Khurasan scheme used a large army of recruits who were paid a year's salary in advance, and it ended without achieving any conquest.

 

NOTE

 

• Khurasan expedition (Option 1): The Khurasan expedition was a real project of 1339-40, for which a huge army was raised and paid a year's salary in advance, so it is one of his schemes.

 

• Token currency (Option 2): Token currency was a genuine project of 1329, in which copper tokens were issued in place of silver coins, and thus it is a project of this Sultan.

 

• Taxation in the Doab (Option 4): Taxation in the Doab was one of his projects, raising the land revenue between the Ganga and the Yamuna during famine, so it is attributed to him.

question: Which of the following is NOT associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Construction of the Alai Darwaza.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Alai Darwaza was built by Alauddin Khalji, not by Firoz Shah Tughlaq (अलाई दरवाज़ा — अलाउद्दीन ख़िलजी)

 

• Firoz Shah founded cities such as Firozabad, Hisar and Fatehabad and built Firoz Shah Kotla in 1354.

 

• He set up welfare departments including Diwan-i-Khairat, Diwan-i-Shifa and Diwan-i-Istiaq.

 

• He reconstructed the fourth storey of the Qutub Minar and added the fifth.

 

• The Alai Darwaza stands at the Qutub complex in Mehrauli and is often cited as an early example of the true arch and dome in India under the Delhi Sultanate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fatehabad was named after his son Fateh Khan.

 

• He also set up Diwan-i-Bandagan for slaves.

 

• The Alai Darwaza is the southern gate to the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

 

• Firoz Shah's capital city of Firozabad lay near Delhi.

 

• Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad and Siri are among the cities of medieval Delhi, built by different rulers.

 

NOTE

 

• Founding of Fatehabad (Option 1): Fatehabad in Haryana was founded by Firoz Shah and named after his son Fateh Khan, so it is connected to him and cannot be the answer.

 

• Founding of Hisar (Option 2): Hisar in Haryana was founded by Firoz Shah as one of his cities, so it is associated with him and is not the correct answer.

 

• Diwan-i-Khairat (Option 3): Diwan-i-Khairat, which gave donations for marriages and the poor, was one of Firoz Shah's welfare departments and is therefore connected with him.

question: Which of the following was NOT a ruler of the Sayyid dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahlol Lodi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bahlol Lodi founded the Lodi dynasty in 1451 and was not a Sayyid ruler (सैयद वंश — खिज्र खाँ, मुबारक शाह, मुहम्मद शाह, आलम शाह)

 

• The Sayyid dynasty (1414-51) had four rulers: Khizr Khan, Mubarak Shah, Muhammad Shah and Alauddin Alam Shah.

 

• Alam Shah gave up the throne in favour of Bahlol Lodi.

 

• Khizr Khan had been appointed governor of Multan by Timur.

 

• The question is best solved by recalling the sequence of dynasties: the Sayyids came after the Tughlaqs, and the Lodis took over only when the last Sayyid, Alam Shah, abdicated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sayyids were a weak dynasty with limited territory.

 

• Bahlol Lodi ruled 1451-89 and founded the first Afghan dynasty.

 

• Sikandar Lodi succeeded Bahlol.

 

• Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan.

 

• Ibrahim Lodi, who ruled 1517-26, was the last Sultan of Delhi and the last of the Lodi dynasty. The Lodi line began with Bahlol, passed to Sikandar in 1489 and ended with Ibrahim at Panipat in 1526.

 

NOTE

 

• Khizr Khan (Option 2): Khizr Khan was the first Sayyid ruler, ruling 1414-21, after Timur had left him in charge of Multan, so he is certainly a Sayyid ruler.

 

• Mubarak Shah (Option 3): Mubarak Shah, son of Khizr Khan, succeeded him in 1421 and so belongs to the Sayyid dynasty, which makes him the wrong choice for this question.

 

• Muhammad Shah (Option 4): Muhammad Shah was the third Sayyid ruler, who succeeded Mubarak Shah in the 1430s, so he belongs to the dynasty and is not the answer.
